data.title: Tejon Ranch Earnings Call Shows Growth and Challenges
data.description:
Tejon Ranch ((TRC)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Tejon Ranch delivered a broadly positive third quarter, with gains in revenue, net income, adjusted EBITDA, mineral resources, occupancy and multifamily activity. Management nevertheless cautioned that unusual timing items, higher net debt, cash-consuming operations and a demanding cost structure mean the transformation is still underway.

Revenue and Earnings Improve

Third-quarter revenue, net income and adjusted EBITDA all exceeded last year’s levels, while year-to-date results were comparable. Net income attributable to common stockholders rose to $3.3 million, or $0.12 per share, from $1.7 million, or $0.06 per share, a year earlier.

Adjusted EBITDA Nearly Doubles

Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $10.4 million from $5.3 million, reflecting stronger performance across much of the operating portfolio. Trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA also climbed about 44% to $35 million from $24.3 million.

Mineral Resources Lead Operating Growth

Mineral Resources revenue increased 25%, while operating income rose nearly 58%, making the segment a major contributor to the quarter’s improvement. National Cement also exercised a 20-year lease extension, continuing a longstanding relationship and supporting the property’s long-term value.

Commercial Portfolio Remains Well Occupied

Tejon Ranch’s commercial and industrial assets maintained high occupancy, with industrial properties fully leased and commercial occupancy at 95%. The results point to continued demand for the company’s strategically located real estate portfolio.

Terra Vista Leasing Gains Momentum

Leasing progress at Terra Vista helped lift multifamily revenue to $924,000 from $181,000 last year. The increase highlights the growing contribution from the apartment business, although construction spending on the project remains an important use of cash.

Lower Corporate Costs and Better Farming Results

Corporate expenses, including share-based compensation adjustments, fell 40% during the quarter and 22% year to date after excluding prior-year non-recurring costs. Adjusted farming EBITDA before fixed water obligations increased to $2.6 million from $425,000, aided by stronger agricultural results.

Commerce Center Construction Advances

Commerce Center Building 1B, being developed with Dedeaux Properties, remains under construction and is progressing toward completion early next year. Management described the joint venture as a capital-efficient model that uses third-party equity and targets strong returns, a structure it hopes to repeat.

Hard Rock Expansion Supports Development Plans

The Tejon Indian Tribe and Hard Rock International broke ground on the next phase of Hard Rock Casino Tejon, including a 406-room hotel and entertainment venue. Management expects the investment to broaden the customer base and create a wider positive impact across the Commerce Center.

Water Sales and Agricultural Timing Affect Results

Tejon Ranch sold a substantial portion of its water before the market changed sharply after a strong El Niño winter, while management said it remains positioned to respond when future demand allows. An early wine-grape harvest shifted sales into the third quarter, and warm spring weather affected almond sizing, with the effect on total yield to be reported at year-end.

Residential Entitlements Move Forward

Kern County approved an amendment to the Grapevine Specific Plan, updating the land-use mix and phasing and moving the project closer to mapping and its first phase reaching the market. At Centennial, the company is processing an updated application before reviews by the Regional Planning Commission and Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors.

Capital Search Continues for Tejon Mountain Village

The fully entitled Tejon Mountain Village remains in the capitalization process as Tejon Ranch seeks investment partners with assistance from outside investment banking resources. The effort is part of management’s broader attempt to turn land holdings into recurring income and improve capital efficiency.

Liquidity Provides Financial Flexibility

The company ended September with approximately $74.4 million of liquidity, including $8.8 million in cash and marketable securities and $65.6 million available under its revolving credit facility. Total debt was $94.4 million, equal to about 16% of total capitalization, although management emphasized that interest expense remains significant.

Operating Cash Flow Improves

Tejon Ranch generated more than $7 million in operating cash this year, compared with about $4 million consumed in the prior year, an improvement of roughly $11 million. Excluding Terra Vista apartment construction, cash use was approximately $14 million lower than a year ago.

One-Time Items Lifted Quarterly Comparisons

Management said the earnings improvement included timing and non-recurring effects, including a second-quarter land-sale contribution from the Dedeaux industrial joint venture, $3.9 million of crop insurance proceeds and $2.6 million of bonus price adjustments tied to last year’s pistachio crop. These items make the quarter stronger but less representative of underlying recurring performance.

Debt and Cost Structure Remain Concerns

Net debt increased $16 million year to date, even though actual borrowings rose only $500,000, with debt reductions expected to follow cash-generating activities. Management acknowledged that some businesses generate cash while others, along with corporate overhead, consume it, and agreed that further cost reductions are needed.

Transformation Requires Capital Discipline

Management is seeking to build a more effective land-company model around Tejon Ranch’s location between Northern and Southern California and the Commerce Center’s industrial, retail, multifamily and travel-center network. It also acknowledged that revenue must rise while controllable costs and discretionary capital spending fall, helping convert assets into durable cash flow.

Share Price Valuation Remains a Frustration

Management said the shares trade below its view of the intrinsic value of the company’s assets, a concern shared by investors. Narrowing that gap will require disciplined capital deployment, stronger recurring cash flow, lower costs and better conversion of land assets into operating returns.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Building 1B remains on track for completion early next year, while Grapevine moves toward mapping and its first phase reaching the market. Centennial is expected to undergo county reviews in the coming months, and the company will continue seeking capital partners for Tejon Mountain Village while working to reduce debt, costs and discretionary capital spending, increase revenue and report fourth-quarter results early next year.

Overall, Tejon Ranch posted meaningful operating improvements, led by higher EBITDA, mineral resources performance, occupancy and multifamily revenue. The gains were tempered by one-time items, rising net debt and cash-flow challenges, leaving investors focused on whether management can turn development assets into recurring income while maintaining disciplined spending.

data.title: EDAP TMS Earnings Call Shows Growth Despite Delays
data.description:
Edap Tms S.A. ((FOCL)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

EDAP TMS delivered a largely positive third quarter, supported by 26% revenue growth, stronger U.S. procedure volumes, improved gross margin and a substantially higher cash balance. However, delayed system sales pushed revenue below expectations, while operating expenses and the operating loss increased; management called the delays timing-related and remained confident in fourth-quarter execution.

HIFU Revenue Growth

Third-quarter HIFU revenue rose 26% to approximately $9.8 million from $7.8 million a year earlier. Growth reflected seven Focal One system sales, compared with six in the prior-year quarter, and a 24% increase in treatment-driven Focal One revenue.

Focal One Install Base Expands

FocalTherics recorded seven global Focal One capital system sales and one net operating lease placement during the quarter. The worldwide installed base reached 192 systems, including 98 in the U.S. and 94 internationally.

Healthcare System Adoption Broadens

Baylor Scott & White purchased its second Focal One system, lifting the number of U.S. hospital networks with at least two systems to 16. The company also entered Maine through MaineHealth Pen Bay Hospital and expanded Kaiser Permanente’s program to four systems through two new leases.

International Commercial Momentum

FocalTherics completed two system sales in Turkey, bringing the country’s total to three, and added sales in Mexico and France. Management said universal French National Health System coverage for Focal One became effective January 1, 2026, supporting capital purchases in that market.

U.S. Procedure Volumes Accelerate

U.S. Focal One procedure volumes increased 32% year over year in the third quarter, more than twice the 15% growth recorded in the same period of 2025. Management said the result was consistent with expectations and normal third-quarter seasonality.

Gross Margin Improves

Gross margin rose to 51.4% from 46.6%, an improvement of 482 basis points. The increase was mainly driven by lower standard costs for the Focal One system and higher average selling prices for Focal One systems and Focalpaks.

Net Loss Narrows

Third-quarter net loss improved to $4.5 million, or $0.10 per share, from $5.9 million, or $0.16 per share, a year earlier. The result benefited from a $2.6 million non-cash gain tied to the fair value of European Investment Bank warrants and $0.5 million in foreign exchange gains.

Cash Position Strengthens

Cash and cash equivalents climbed to $56.3 million at the end of the third quarter from $21.5 million in the second quarter. The increase reflected proceeds from the company’s August equity raise, which management said leaves EDAP financially positioned to pursue its strategic priorities.

Reimbursement and Clinical Support Expand

The HIFI-2 study showed meaningful cancer control for patients receiving Focal One robotic HIFU after primary radiation had failed. HIFU gained a Category 2A recommendation from the NCCN for this population, while several major and regional insurers issued coverage policies for salvage treatment.

Physician Education Gains Momentum

During Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, FocalTherics partnered with the Chicago Urological Society on a sold-out symposium attended by 70 physicians from 35 institutions across 14 states. The company also participated in FOCAL+ 2026 and the DGU Congress to promote peer education and knowledge sharing.

BPH and Endometriosis Programs Advance

The company is continuing its BPH clinical program in Chile with urologists from the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and reported encouraging early results. For deep infiltrating endometriosis, three European centers are treating commercial patients, while additional sites in the U.K. and France are completing training.

HIFUSA Study Progresses

The Phase III randomized HIFUSA trial comparing Focal One with active surveillance has enrolled 108 patients across 14 centers. Management said preliminary feedback has been positive, while emphasizing that the early findings remain unverified.

Technology Investment Continues

FocalTherics said it is advancing its Focal One technology roadmap through investments in Focal Connect, artificial intelligence and histotripsy. The company is also continuing to build clinical evidence intended to support broader reimbursement and insurance coverage.

Industry Recognition

FocalTherics received the Innovation Champion Award at the European Investment Bank TechEU Equity Summit 2026 in Luxembourg. The award highlights external recognition of the company’s technology and development efforts.

Pipeline Supports Fourth-Quarter Momentum

Management described the active pipeline as strong across both U.S. and international markets. Of the three systems delayed from the third quarter, one had closed and purchase orders had been signed for the other two early in the fourth quarter.

Revenue Miss Reflects Delayed Sales

Third-quarter revenue came in below expectations because three anticipated Focal One system sales did not close by quarter-end. Management attributed the delays to hospital value-analysis and committee reviews, summer seasonality in capital purchasing and one transaction becoming tied up with a financing bank.

Full-Year Guidance Narrowed

EDAP narrowed its 2026 revenue guidance to $50 million-$52 million from $50 million-$54 million previously. The revised range still implies growth of 34%-39% over 2025, but reflects a more cautious view after the three delayed systems were excluded from third-quarter revenue.

Operating Expenses Increase

Operating expenses rose to $12.8 million from $10.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. Higher headcount-related compensation, including stock-based compensation, and added sales and marketing costs for urology meetings contributed to the increase, lifting the operating loss to $7.8 million from $6.7 million.

Financing Costs Weigh on Results

The improvement in net loss was partly offset by a $1.1 million incremental operating loss and $0.4 million of interest expense. Both costs were associated with the Tranche A and Tranche B drawdowns.

Procedure Ramp Requires Time

Management cautioned that procedure volumes should build moderately because hospitals need time to install systems and train personnel. Developing a sustainable program also takes time as new accounts are added and clinical teams become familiar with the technology.

Guidance Points to Stronger Fourth Quarter

Management expects 2026 revenue of $50 million-$52 million, with the three delayed systems now expected to contribute in the fourth quarter; one has closed and two have signed purchase orders. The company expects to finish strongly, maintain consistent procedure growth and complete final HIFUSA follow-up in the first quarter, with publication expected early next year.

EDAP TMS enters the final quarter with expanding adoption, improving margins, stronger reimbursement support and a solid cash cushion. Although delayed sales and rising costs remain concerns, management framed the revenue timing issue as temporary and pointed to a growing commercial and clinical pipeline as support for its longer-term outlook.

data.title: Celsius Holdings Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Challenges
data.description:
Celsius Holdings ((CELH)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Celsius Holdings delivered a broadly upbeat third-quarter earnings call, led by strong portfolio revenue growth, record Alani Nu results, international momentum and better operating leverage. Investors also heard clear challenges, including declines at CELSIUS and Rockstar, weaker gross margins, elevated commodity costs and a tougher fourth-quarter comparison.

Revenue Growth Accelerates

Celsius Holdings reported third-quarter revenue of approximately $847 million, a 17% increase from the prior year. The result showed continued expansion despite pressure in parts of the company’s brand portfolio.

Portfolio Gains Energy Share

The combined portfolio held about 21% of the energy category in tracked U.S. channels, equal to roughly one in five energy drinks purchased. Modern energy brands also contributed approximately 28% of zero-sugar energy category growth during the quarter.

Retail Sales Continue to Expand

Portfolio retail sales in tracked channels rose approximately 15% year over year, matching the second-quarter pace. Management said the brands continued attracting new consumers and creating additional occasions for energy drink consumption.

Alani Nu Posts a Record Quarter

Alani Nu delivered its strongest quarter since launch, with net sales of approximately $410 million, up 24% year over year. Retail sales in tracked channels climbed approximately 58%, showing accelerating momentum for the fast-growing brand.

Witch’s Brew Becomes a Breakout Hit

The Witch’s Brew limited-time offer generated more than $130 million in retail sales across traditional retail and club channels. Core 12-ounce sales were nearly 80% above last year, while its peak week was the biggest for any Celsius Holdings item.

Alani Nu Growth Extends Beyond One Product

Excluding Witch’s Brew, core Alani Nu retail sales in tracked channels increased approximately 50% year over year. The company is moving successful limited-time flavors into its permanent lineup, and management said the program sold through well at retail.

Alani Nu Gains Category Share

Alani Nu’s tracked-channel category share reached approximately 9.8%, nearly three points higher than a year earlier. Management said the brand remains under-penetrated in channels where the broader portfolio already has a strong presence.

Rockstar Shows Signs of Stabilization

Rockstar was stable sequentially, with remaining carried-forward SKUs within about 1% of the prior year in the third quarter. Its year-over-year trend has improved every quarter since acquisition, and more than twice as many states were growing compared with the end of last year.

Rockstar Productivity Improves

Rockstar net sales increased to approximately $80 million from $67 million in the second quarter. Dollars per point of distribution rose about 14% sequentially as the company concentrated on a more focused assortment.

New Brand-Led Structure Takes Shape

Celsius Holdings created three brand-led business units covering CELSIUS, Alani Nu, and Rockstar and Emerging Growth. Each unit will have a dedicated president, with Alex Zigliara leading Brand CELSIUS in the U.S. and Rishi Daing taking an expanded role at Rockstar.

Innovation Pipeline Builds Toward 2027

Management highlighted significant planned innovation across CELSIUS and Alani Nu, including new flavors, product lines and permanent SKUs. Celsius Spritz Vibe Sparkling Shirley Temple was already on shelves, while additional CELSIUS products and Alani Nu Winter Wonderland were scheduled for upcoming launches.

CELSIUS Prepares for a Turnaround

Brand CELSIUS performed in line with management’s expectations, although it is not yet at the desired level. The company said its core national SKU lineup is established, retailers are planning earlier and innovation will play a larger role in restoring momentum.

International Revenue Surges

Revenue outside the U.S. increased approximately 56% year over year in the third quarter. Management expects international markets to account for more than 15% of total revenue over the next five years, increasing the company’s exposure beyond the domestic market.

European Awareness and Share Improve

Aided brand awareness roughly doubled in both the U.K. and France since early last year. Category share increased year over year in every new European market, driven by broader distribution and higher sales rates rather than pricing.

Australia and New Zealand Gain Momentum

Growth in Australia and New Zealand was well ahead of last year. Orange became the leading CELSIUS flavor in every Australian account, giving the company another encouraging sign in its international expansion efforts.

Manufacturing Projects Target Margin Recovery

A second manufacturing line in North Carolina was operating, although its full benefit is expected later. The company is also pursuing vertical integration, direct sourcing, better case costs for Alani Nu and Rockstar, and revenue management initiatives.

Adjusted EBITDA Benefits From Leverage

Adjusted EBITDA reached approximately $199 million, or 23.4% of revenue, compared with $184 million, or 22.5%, in the second quarter. Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA was $578 million, or about 23.6% of revenue, as operating leverage offset lower gross margin.

SG&A Ratio Moves Lower

Selling, general and administrative expenses totaled $221 million, equal to approximately 26.1% of revenue. That compared with 29% in the second quarter and 28.4% a year earlier, highlighting improved cost discipline as sales expanded.

Share Repurchases Continue

The company repurchased approximately $45 million of stock in the third quarter, bringing year-to-date buybacks to about $169 million. Management said approximately $91 million remained under the $300 million authorization and described the balance sheet as a source of flexibility.

Energy+ Adds New Growth Avenues

Management described Energy+ as incremental to the core business, aimed at attracting consumers and occasions in adjacent energy, fitness, health and wellness categories. Growth will also rely on core flavors, multipacks, new pack sizes and an 8-ounce format.

Alani Nu International Launches Planned

Celsius Holdings was finalizing the international markets where Alani Nu is expected to launch in 2027. The company plans to use market-entry playbooks developed during CELSIUS’s international expansion.

CELSIUS Retail Sales Decline

CELSIUS retail sales in tracked channels fell approximately 7% year over year, while reported net sales declined about 6%. Management attributed the weakness partly to difficult comparisons after last year’s innovation and acknowledged that the brand still needs to improve.

Rockstar Remains in Recovery Mode

Rockstar total retail sales remained below the prior year, with scanner-based sales down approximately 13%. The decline was largely tied to exited items, and management said it was not yet declaring that the brand had returned to growth.

Gross Margin Faces Commodity Pressure

Third-quarter gross margin fell to 46.8% from 48.1% in the second quarter and 51.3% a year earlier. Higher aluminum and diesel costs contributed to the decline, while management said commodity-related margin improvement was taking longer than expected.

Full-Year Margin Seen in the High 40s

Depending on commodity movements, Celsius Holdings expects full-year gross margin to land in the high 40s. Management said a recovery in commodity costs would help the company reach its low-50s margin target sooner.

Alani Nu Mix Raises Trade Investment

Trade investment as a percentage of gross sales increased modestly from the second quarter. Early benefits from pricing architecture and lower slotting fees were outweighed by the Alani Nu mix, including Witch’s Brew, which moved more volume through direct-store delivery.

Fourth-Quarter Comparison Will Be Difficult

The company expects fourth-quarter reported revenue growth to trail the pace set during the first three quarters. The comparison includes a prior-year benefit of about $25 million from inventory activity, $20 million to $25 million of shipments pulled forward into the third quarter and higher trade investment.

Alani Nu Scans Still Exceed Reported Sales

The gap between Alani Nu scanner performance and reported sales remained approximately 24% to 25% in the second and third quarters. Management attributed the difference to direct-store delivery transitions, non-ready-to-drink activity and timing factors, with cleaner comparisons expected next year.

CELSIUS Works Through Distribution Issues

CELSIUS had fewer points of distribution and continued to address planogram sequencing and rationalization. Management also cited quarter-to-quarter volatility related to Amazon timing and the timing of the prior-year limited-time offer.

Aluminum and Diesel Costs Stay Elevated

Aluminum costs remained high on both the London Metal Exchange and Midwest premium, while diesel reached its highest level in several years. Outbound freight was slightly favorable as a percentage of revenue, but that benefit largely offset rather than erased higher diesel costs.

Supply Chain Leadership Transition

The company disclosed the recent passing of Chief Supply Chain Officer Paul Storey. Seth Nicholas assumed the role of Executive Vice President of Operations and interim chief supply chain officer to maintain continuity across supply chain operations.

Guidance Points to Near-Term Pressure and Longer-Term Growth

Management expects fourth-quarter reported revenue growth to be below the pace of the first three quarters, with full-year gross margin in the high 40s depending on commodities. CELSIUS is expected to return to growth across 2027, while innovation, improving trade investment, international expansion and eventual Rockstar growth are expected to support the longer-term outlook.

Celsius Holdings enters the next phase with strong Alani Nu momentum, expanding international sales and improving profitability. However, investors will be watching whether CELSIUS and Rockstar stabilize, margins recover and the company navigates a difficult fourth-quarter comparison.

data.title: Kingsway Corporation Earnings Call Highlights Strong Growth
data.description:
Kingsway Corporation ((KWY)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Kingsway Corporation’s third-quarter earnings call carried a broadly positive tone, led by portfolio EBITDA growth, stronger segment profitability, solid operating cash flow and lower net debt. Those gains outweighed a larger consolidated net loss, weaker consolidated adjusted EBITDA, DDI’s ongoing investment period and a slower expected pace of acquisitions.

Portfolio EBITDA Reaches a New High

Kingsway reported portfolio EBITDA of just over $6 million in the third quarter, a 29% increase from the year-earlier period. Management called it the second-strongest quarter of operating performance since the current CEO began leading the company.

Segment Profitability Improves

KSX adjusted EBITDA rose 24.5% to $3.3 million from $2.7 million a year earlier. Extended Warranty adjusted EBITDA increased 88.3% to $1.4 million, or $1.4 million compared with $400,000 when excluding Trinity.

Organic Growth Builds Momentum

Organic segment revenue growth was approximately 8%, while organic segment adjusted EBITDA growth reached roughly 54%. Management said most operating businesses delivered solid or exceptional year-over-year organic growth, with several units standing out.

KSX Delivers Stronger Revenue

KSX revenue increased 18.2% to $22.4 million from $19 million in the prior-year quarter. The result added to evidence that the segment is converting operating improvements into meaningful top-line expansion.

Extended Warranty Shows Underlying Growth

Extended Warranty revenue fell 9.8% to $16.4 million from $18.2 million, largely reflecting the sale of Trinity. Excluding Trinity, revenue rose 5.9% to $16.4 million and cash sales increased 6.3% during the quarter.

Operating Cash Flow Remains Healthy

Cash generated from operations reached $4.1 million in the quarter. Management attributed the strong conversion of EBITDA into cash to the asset-light nature of Kingsway’s services businesses.

Penn PWI Benefits From Integration

Penn and PWI were consolidated into a single-company culture in 2026, while PWI moved from a legacy 30-year-old system to a modern cloud-based ERP. Management said financial results improved as the year progressed and that significant top-line and bottom-line opportunities remain.

Skilled Trades Returns to Profitability

Kingsway Skilled Trades moved from a loss in the year-ago quarter to profitability in the third quarter. Bud’s continued to perform well, while AAA reduced expenses, improved KPI tracking and strengthened marketing processes through the Kingsway Business System.

Southside Completes Troubled Project

Southside completed the legacy one-off construction project that had led to repeated write-downs. Its team is now being redeployed toward work that management views as more profitable and consistent.

SNS Moves Back Into the Black

SNS also returned to profitability after reporting a loss in the year-ago period. A streamlined cloud-based IT environment, clearer operating procedures, better cash collection and efforts to win more per diem and travel nurse assignments supported the improvement.

DDI Continues Platform Investment

DDI invested in technology and operations aimed at building a scalable platform with strong reliability, accuracy and response times. It also expanded its sales force, with management saying the sales funnel was developing well despite the near-term cost burden.

Long-Term Organic Growth Target

Management’s long-term objective is consistent double-digit organic segment adjusted EBITDA growth. The Kingsway Business System, which focuses on operating discipline and execution, is intended to support that objective across the portfolio.

Trailing Portfolio EBITDA Advances

LTM portfolio EBITDA rose to between $23 million and $24 million as of September 30, 2026. Management expressed confidence in the metric’s continued positive trajectory, supported by operating momentum across the portfolio.

RCC Integration Progresses

Image Solutions completed its acquisition of Romeo Computer Company in August. The transaction was financed entirely at the Image Solutions level without additional equity from Kingsway, and management said RCC was performing well with integration on track.

Acquisition Pipeline Remains Active

Kingsway reported numerous indications of interest, letters of intent and management meetings in recent weeks and months. The company also developed an artificial-intelligence-enabled process to source, screen, score and assign opportunities across roughly 10,000 brokers and intermediaries.

Net Debt Moves Lower

Total net debt declined to $60.3 million as of September 30, 2026, from $62.4 million at the end of 2025. The reduction gives Kingsway additional financial flexibility while it continues to invest in operations and acquisitions.

Platforms Move Toward Self-Funding

Management said platform businesses can increasingly fund tuck-in acquisitions as operators gain experience, reduce leverage and build cash. That capacity typically develops around the second or third year, with Image Solutions cited as an example.

Business System Shows Broad Benefits

Kingsway said its core operating pillars—including leadership, data and daily management, talent, enterprise excellence, planning and growth—are broadly applicable across its businesses. Management believes those practices are contributing to better execution and profitability.

Consolidated Net Loss Widens

Despite stronger operating results in several businesses, consolidated net loss increased to $3.2 million from $2.4 million in the prior-year quarter. The result reflected corporate items and other factors that offset portfolio-level progress.

Consolidated EBITDA Edges Down

Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $2 million, compared with $2.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The modest decline contrasted with the stronger performance of the operating segments and highlighted the impact of corporate and investment items.

DDI Remains a Key Headwind

DDI continued to weigh on results and remained in its J-curve phase, during which investment precedes expected earnings benefits. Additional sales-force costs were incurred ahead of new business implementations, adding pressure to the quarter.

Acquisition Throughput Slows

Kingsway’s acquisition pace was reduced after two Operators-in-Residence moved into leadership roles at SNS and Kingsway Skilled Trades. In addition, several tuck-in opportunities failed during later-stage diligence, limiting completed transactions.

Argo Investment Values Decline

Argo recorded a $900,000 net decrease in the value of its remaining investments during the quarter. Higher debt levels at certain investees reduced their fair values; excluding this item, consolidated EBITDA would have been $2.9 million.

Revenue Re-Deferrals Affect Results

Kingsway recorded approximately $600,000 of non-cash revenue re-deferrals at operating subsidiaries, with the largest effects at SPI and Penn PWI. Management described the combination of several large re-deferrals in one quarter as unusual.

Management Maintains Growth Outlook

Kingsway expects organic profit growth to remain strong in the fourth quarter and into 2027, while targeting consistent double-digit organic segment adjusted EBITDA growth over time. Management also expects LTM portfolio EBITDA to maintain its positive trajectory from the current $23 million-to-$24 million range.

Acquisition Outlook Becomes More Measured

Management said it is increasingly likely that Kingsway will complete two deals rather than three in 2026. The company continues to target three to five deals annually in 2027, while platform-level tuck-in capacity may increasingly become self-funding around years two to three.

Overall, Kingsway’s call showed meaningful operating progress, with stronger EBITDA, organic growth, cash generation and profitability at several businesses. The wider net loss, DDI investment costs, unusual re-deferrals and slower deal activity remain risks, but management presented a portfolio that is becoming more operationally disciplined and financially resilient.

data.title: Algonquin Power Earnings Call Signals Progress Amid Challenges
data.description:
Algonquin Power ((TSE:AQN)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Algonquin Power’s earnings call carried a largely positive tone as management highlighted stronger adjusted earnings, stable liquidity, regulatory progress and a simplified portfolio. However, lower GAAP profit, higher operating and wildfire insurance costs, Missouri uncertainties and ongoing execution challenges remained important concerns for investors.

Adjusted Earnings Gained Ground

Algonquin reported third-quarter adjusted earnings attributable to common shareholders of $88.1 million, up from $69.0 million a year earlier. Adjusted net EPS rose by $0.02 to $0.11, supported by favorable Empire Electric weather, new rates and a $7.1 million tax and noncontrolling-interest benefit.

Year-to-Date Adjusted Results Improved

Year-to-date adjusted earnings increased to $216.9 million from $211.6 million. The main drivers included $45.3 million from the CalPeco rate case, $13.3 million from rate adjustments and customer growth elsewhere, and an $11.2 million benefit from favorable weather.

EPS Outlook Reaffirmed

Management reaffirmed adjusted net EPS guidance of $0.35 to $0.37 for 2026 and $0.38 to $0.42 for 2027. The targets signal confidence that rate recovery, operational improvements and portfolio actions can support earnings growth.

Missouri Large-Load Tariff Filed

Empire Electric Missouri filed a large-load tariff designed to support economic development and serve potential major customers. Management said the proposal would protect residential and small-business customers by requiring large-load users to pay their representative cost of service.

Transmission Incentives Support Investment

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission granted CWIP and abandonment incentives for Empire’s transmission projects in the Southwest Power Pool. Algonquin said the incentives fit its strategy of investing in assets that improve reliability for customers.

Suralis Sale Simplified the Portfolio

Algonquin completed the sale of its 64% interest in Chilean water utility Suralis for $126 million of proceeds. The transaction also removed Suralis debt from the balance sheet and was described as slightly credit positive, while a tax benefit made its 2026 impact largely neutral.

Arizona Rate Case Reached Resolution

The company reached what management called a constructive resolution of the Litchfield Park Water and Sewer rate case in Arizona. The agreement includes a formula-rate provision, giving the utility a mechanism intended to better align rates with its cost and investment needs.

Regulatory Activity Remains High

Algonquin filed new rate cases at Empire Electric Oklahoma and Granite State Electric while also securing the Litchfield Park decision. Management said the proceedings are intended to recover investments needed to serve customers safely and reliably.

Liquidity and Leverage Stayed Conservative

Algonquin reported $1.2 billion of liquidity and maintained a BBB credit rating. HoldCo debt of $1.4 billion represented about 20% of consolidated debt, below the 25% to 30% level cited for comparable peers, supporting management’s financing plans.

Interest Rate Risk Was Hedged

The company said it effectively hedged interest rate exposure on its hybrid notes. Management expects the move to provide greater certainty around financing costs at the holding-company level.

U.S. Redomicile Moving Ahead

Algonquin said its planned move of domicile to the United States remains on track for the first half of 2027. Management estimates the completed transaction could reduce cross-border tax friction and add $0.02 to $0.03 to annualized adjusted net EPS.

Cost Programs Are Producing Savings

Outsourcing, application rationalization and lower IT spending have reduced costs, according to management. The company is continuing to target O&M in the low to mid-30s as a percentage of gross revenue, although further work is needed.

Missouri Stakeholder Engagement Continues

Management said the Missouri tariff filing followed discussions with the governor, legislature, customer groups and the commission. It also pointed to Senate Bill 4 as providing customer protections and said early stakeholder reaction had been encouraging.

Missouri Revenue Opportunity Remains Open

Algonquin continues working to resolve a potential $13.7 million of annualized Missouri revenue. Management said it had addressed billing and other issues behind earlier underperformance and was encouraged by improved customer outcomes.

GAAP Earnings Declined

Third-quarter GAAP earnings attributable to common shareholders fell to $57.6 million from $71.0 million a year earlier. The decline contrasted with the increase in adjusted earnings and reflected higher costs and the absence of prior-year benefits.

Year-to-Date GAAP Profit Fell

Year-to-date GAAP earnings declined to $145.6 million from $178.6 million in the prior-year period. The comparison was affected by one-time items and other adjustments that did not recur in the latest results.

Higher Costs Weighed on Comparisons

Third-quarter results absorbed $4.4 million of higher operating expenses tied to gas safety, labor and maintenance. They also lacked a favorable $7.1 million EnergyNorth depreciation deferral recorded in the prior year, while year-to-date results faced $29.7 million of nonrecurring-item comparisons.

Gas Expenses Increased

Year-to-date operating, depreciation and other expenses rose by $29 million. Higher gas operating expenses accounted for most of the increase, adding $24.8 million and underscoring the pressure on the company’s cost base.

Wildfire Insurance Created a Headwind

The benefit from new rates was partly offset by wildfire insurance costs and lower GSEP revenue at New England Gas. CalPeco also recorded an additional accrual for wildfire insurance covering the 2025 period and year-to-date 2026.

O&M Improvement Is Still Incomplete

Some severance and consulting costs tied to continuous-improvement programs were excluded from adjusted earnings but remained in the O&M line. Management said the cost curve still needs to move further toward the low to mid-30s as a percentage of gross revenue.

Large-Load Plans Need Approval

The Missouri opportunity depends on commission approval of the filed tariff. Management did not disclose potential customer commitments, saying related work would remain private unless all parties agreed to release details.

Missouri Billing Issues Required Remediation

Management acknowledged that billing and other customer-service problems had contributed to Missouri underperformance. The company is working to improve outcomes, while discussions continue over the potential $13.7 million of annualized revenue and additional visibility is expected in the coming months.

Redomicile Has Conditions

The proposed U.S. redomicile remains subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals, along with other customary conditions. The expected tax benefit therefore depends on completing the transaction and meeting those requirements.

Execution Remains the Main Test

Management emphasized that considerable work remains and that the transformation will not proceed in a straight line. Improving operational performance, customer service, regulatory relationships and earned returns will be central to converting the company’s plans into consistent results.

Forward Guidance

Algonquin expects adjusted net EPS of $0.35 to $0.37 in 2026 and $0.38 to $0.42 in 2027, and does not expect to issue equity through 2027 to fund current plans. It is also targeting lower O&M, expects the redomicile in the first half of 2027, and sees a potential $13.7 million Missouri revenue opportunity, with about half available this year and guidance assuming reasonable outcomes.

Algonquin’s call presented a company making progress on earnings, regulation, financing and portfolio simplification. Still, investors will be watching GAAP pressure, operating-cost reduction, Missouri approvals and execution closely as management works to turn its improving adjusted performance into more durable growth.

data.title: Sturm, Ruger Earnings Call Signals Stronger Growth Ahead
data.description:
Sturm, Ruger & Company, Inc. ((RGR)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Sturm, Ruger & Company delivered a broadly positive earnings call, highlighted by stronger sales, sharply improved profitability and a debt-free balance sheet. Management also pointed to record near-term production and healthy distributor inventories, while acknowledging weaker demand in some categories, lower product-mix pricing and the exit or suspension of select product families.

Sales Growth Accelerates

Third-quarter net sales reached $148 million, up 17% from $127 million a year earlier. Management also reported both year-over-year and sequential sales growth, signaling improving momentum across the business.

Profitability Improves Significantly

Adjusted EBITDA rose to $14 million from $3 million in the prior-year quarter, producing a 10% margin. Management credited favorable product mix, continued premiumization within existing families and better manufacturing efficiency for the improvement.

Earnings Per Share Rises

Diluted earnings increased to $0.36 per share from $0.10 in the year-earlier period. Adjusted diluted earnings also climbed to $0.44 per share, showing that the stronger operating performance translated into meaningful bottom-line gains.

First Nine Months Show Double-Digit Growth

Net sales for the first nine months totaled $447 million, representing a 13% increase from the same period in 2025. The result reinforces management’s view that the company is operating from a stronger sales base than it had a year ago.

Debt-Free Balance Sheet Supports Returns

Ruger generated $24 million in operating cash flow during the first nine months, while cash and short-term investments stood at $101 million at quarter-end. With no debt and a 3-to-1 current ratio, the company also declared a $0.18 quarterly dividend and returned $6.4 million through dividends.

Factory Investment Lifts Output

The company continued modernizing its manufacturing network and adding capacity where backlog supported investment. Management described quarterly production as a near-term record, driven by product rationalization, better planning, greater mix flexibility and stronger employee alignment across facilities.

New Systems Bring Greater Discipline

Ruger implemented its new Oracle Enterprise platform during the quarter and continued expanding the Ruger Business System. Management said the tools are improving access to information, business processes and accountability, helping the company make faster and more disciplined operating decisions.

Portfolio Focus Creates Room To Innovate

Management is reducing product complexity and aligning people, equipment and capital with markets offering stronger demand, profitability and long-term potential. The rationalization is also creating capacity for product innovation, with numerous new models expected to support the company’s growth strategy.

Progress Reported On 2026 Priorities

Management said it made measurable progress on five priorities: improving profitability, matching factory capacity with demand, resizing the business for its future portfolio, increasing output on proven high-demand lines and entering new markets through complete product ecosystems. The initiatives are intended to make the company more efficient and focused.

Distributor Inventories Remain Healthy

Ruger described its backlog as healthy and distributor inventory as satisfactory. Management also viewed third-quarter consumer demand positively, saying distributors entered the fall and holiday periods with an inventory position that was generally in balance.

New Product Process Moves Forward

The company said its efforts to align the new-product-development process were progressing well. Management indicated that planned launches over the next three to four months remained on track, supported by coordinated marketing and sales programs.

Headcount Actions Add Savings

Savings from workforce actions taken earlier in the year are now flowing through the business and are expected to continue doing so. Management said the affected positions were not replaced, allowing resources to be redirected toward new-product development and other strategic priorities.

Capital Spending Plan Holds

Ruger spent $9 million on capital expenditures during the first nine months. Despite its manufacturing modernization efforts, management maintained its expectation for approximately $30 million in capital spending for the full year.

Some Product Families Face Exit

The company suspended production of a limited number of product families and plans to complete final 2026 production and allocation for several others. Together, these products account for about 4% of unit production, or roughly $25 million in revenue, but generate minimal to no profitability.

Product Mix Pressures Average Selling Price

The average selling price of units ordered was below expectations and historical levels during the quarter. Management attributed the decline mainly to product mix and shipment timing, characterizing it as a short-term issue rather than a broad deterioration in pricing power.

Weak Categories Prompt Difficult Choices

Demand in some product categories was low enough to lead to production suspensions and portfolio changes. Management acknowledged that some gun owners were unhappy about pauses to heritage product lines, but said it was listening to customers and responding to current demand for other products.

Guidance: Investment And Launches Remain On Track

Ruger expects full-year capital expenditures of approximately $30 million and plans to proceed with the previously announced product-family suspensions and final 2026 allocations. Management also expects numerous new and innovative models over the coming months, with launches planned within the next three to four months and progress toward its targeted annual and quarterly product output.

Overall, the earnings call presented a company with improving sales, stronger margins, solid cash generation and a flexible balance sheet. Ruger is balancing that progress with selective product exits and category weakness, using portfolio discipline, factory investment and innovation to sharpen its business for the next stage.

data.title: Eton Pharmaceuticals Earnings Call Highlights Record Growth
data.description:
Eton Pharmaceuticals ((ETON)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Eton Pharmaceuticals’ Earnings Call Signals Strong Growth and Pipeline Expansion

The tone of Eton Pharmaceuticals’ earnings call was strongly positive, led by record revenue, wider margins, profitability and robust operating cash flow. Management also highlighted stronger patient demand and a broader late-stage pipeline, while noting challenges including ET-700’s weaker efficacy than GALZIN, rising expenses, a planned ALKINDI milestone payment and regulatory dependencies.

Record Revenue and Patient Growth

Eton’s third-quarter revenue surged 158% year over year to $57.9 million from $22.5 million. Growth was supported by a full quarter of HEMANGEOL sales and higher revenue from INCRELEX, ALKINDI SPRINKLE, KHINDIVI, DESMODA, GALZIN and Carglumic Acid.

Broad-Based Commercial Momentum

Active patient counts reached record levels across all major branded products, including INCRELEX, HEMANGEOL, ALKINDI SPRINKLE, KHINDIVI, GALZIN and DESMODA. Eton also exceeded its $200 million annualized revenue goal five quarters ahead of its 2027 target, reflecting faster-than-expected commercial execution.

Margins and Profitability Expand Sharply

Adjusted EBITDA climbed to $28.5 million, or 49% of revenue, from $2.9 million, or 13%, a year earlier, even after a $3 million ASN-001 licensing payment. Adjusted gross profit reached $46.2 million, producing an 80% adjusted gross margin versus 45% last year.

Net Income and Cash Flow Strengthen

Eton posted net income of $35.2 million, or $1.06 per diluted share, compared with a prior-year loss of $1.9 million. Non-GAAP net income rose to $16.5 million, while operating cash flow reached $35 million and helped lift cash to $55.6 million after a $5 million debt prepayment.

HEMANGEOL Builds on Relaunch

The quarter included three full months of HEMANGEOL sales following its May 1 relaunch, and Eton said it had both retained the historical base of about 8,000 patients and moved above that level. Net pricing was near or slightly above the prior $8,000 to $10,000 range, supported by a better product mix.

LIBERVANT Adds a Focused Growth Opportunity

Eton licensed LIBERVANT, an orphan-designated buccal film for seizure clusters, targeting a U.S. rescue-treatment market exceeding $450 million annually. The company plans a highly targeted commercial model centered on roughly 2,000 pediatric neurologists, likely using a sales force of fewer than 20 people.

Pipeline Expansion Raises Long-Term Potential

Eton’s pipeline now contains nine programs, including three that could launch in 2027 and four viewed by management as having more than $100 million in revenue potential. Management said ASN-001, HEMANGEOL and LIBERVANT have lifted its expectations and could bring the $500 million 2030 revenue goal forward.

ET-900 Opens a Large Rare-Disease Opportunity

The company licensed Baylor College of Medicine patents for ET-900, which uses the active ingredient in INCRELEX to treat infantile spasms. A Phase II investigator-led study is planned, with management estimating that proof-of-concept investment could be below $1 million and that a successful product could eventually generate hundreds of millions of dollars annually.

ET-700 Shows Safety Benefits but Lower Efficacy

In a three-arm study, treatment-related adverse events occurred in one of 12 ET-700 patients versus eight of 12 GALZIN patients, supporting the potential for better tolerability. However, ET-700 reduced copper absorption less effectively than GALZIN, likely because its eight-hour release profile was too slow, leaving faster formulations to be tested.

ASN-001 Targets Underserved Infants

Eton completed its ASN-001 licensing transaction and said the product could treat infants with moderate hemangiomas who are not candidates for systemic HEMANGEOL. Management also cited potentially favorable Medicaid rebate dynamics and said ASN-001 could ultimately become the company’s largest product.

Label Expansion Supports Existing Brands

An INCRELEX label-harmonization study has begun and could expand its addressable market by about five times, creating an opportunity management values at more than $100 million in annual revenue. KHINDIVI’s label expansion is under FDA review, while ALKINDI and KHINDIVI continue to grow in their existing forms.

Additional Products Move Toward Filing

Eton completed the bioavailability study for Glyburide Oral Suspension, known as Amglidia in Europe, and is preparing its U.S. filing; the product has fast-track status and no FDA-approved oral treatment currently exists for neonatal diabetes. The company also said recent success has increased inbound deal flow and expanded its ability to pursue larger late-stage or commercial rare-disease assets.

Higher Costs Reflect a Larger Platform

Research and development expenses rose to $5.3 million from $1.1 million, mainly because of the ASN-001 payment and higher Glyburide development costs. General and administrative expense increased 98% to $16 million due to staffing, benefits, stock compensation, broader operating needs and higher FDA fees after the loss of an orphan-drug fee exemption.

Execution Risks Remain

Management still sees meaningful room to convert patients using generic off-label oral formulations to HEMANGEOL and may modestly expand its pediatric dermatology sales force. LIBERVANT’s planned launch also depends on FDA approval and resolution of exclusivity restrictions, while ET-700’s development path depends on results from faster-release formulations.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Eton raised 2026 revenue guidance to more than $175 million from $145 million and lifted adjusted EBITDA margin guidance above 40%, while expecting adjusted gross margin to approach 75%. Management expects margins near 50% in coming quarters, LIBERVANT in April 2027 subject to approvals, ET-900 enrollment in early 2027, ASN-001 launch potential in 2028, and possible 2027 launches for KHINDIVI and Glyburide Oral Suspension.

Eton’s earnings call presented a company moving from growth investment toward strong profitability and cash generation. Record demand, expanding margins, debt reduction and a deeper pipeline outweighed development, cost and regulatory risks, leaving investors with a broadly upbeat view of the company’s commercial trajectory.
